source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1101 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1101 was established by Ordinance No. 32601, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 8, 2023. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1101 is established on property generally bounded by Haskell Avenue on the north and east, the Santa Fe Trail on the south, and Ash Lane on the west. The size of PD 1101 is approximately 2.685 acres. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Purpose And Vision
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.103. PURPOSE AND VISION.

This district is designed to encourage walkable, mixed-use, sustainable, urban development; to reduce the need for parking; and to encourage the use of DART and the Santa Fe Trail. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Definitions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.104. DEFINITIONS.

The definitions in Chapter 51A and Division 51A-13.200 apply to this article. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.105. INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) In general.

(1) Unless otherwise stated, Article XIII, “Form Districts,” of Chapter 51A applies to this article.

(2) Unless otherwise stated, the interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(3) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(b) Conflicts.

(1) If there is a conflict between the provisions of Article XIII and Chapter 51A, Article XIII controls.

(2) If there is a conflict between the provisions of this article and Article XIII, this article controls.

(3) If there is a conflict between the text of this article and any of the exhibits the text of this article controls. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.106 EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 1101A: frontage and open space plan. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Site Plans And Development Plans
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.107 SITE PLANS AND DEVELOPMENT PLANS.

(a) Site plan. Except as provided in this article, a site plan that complies with the requirements of this article and Section 51A-13.703, “Site Plan Review,” must be submitted to the building official when required by Section 51A-13.703(a).

(b) Development plan. No development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply.

(c) Frontage and open space plan. The frontage and open space plan (Exhibit 1101A) depicts street and trail frontages and generalized location of open space and parking. Open space and parking on all future site plans for the Property must be consistent with the frontage and open space plan. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: District Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.108. DISTRICT REGULATIONS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this article, the district regulations for the WMU- 5 Walkable Urban Mixed Use District apply.

(b) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 80 feet.

(2) If compliant with Section 51P-1101.109, the maximum structure height is 120 feet.

(c) Stories.

(1) Minimum. Except for accessory buildings facing the Santa Fe Trail, the minimum number of stories above grade is two. The minimum height provisions of Section 51A- 13.302(b) also apply.

(2) Maximum.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum number of stories above grade is five.

(B) If compliant with Section 51P-1101.109, the maximum number of stories above grade is eight. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Development           Bonuses        For       Mixed     Income
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.109. DEVELOPMENT BONUSES FOR MIXED INCOME HOUSING.

(a) In general. The development bonuses identified in Section 51P-1101.108 apply if a minimum of 10 percent of the total number of units are available to households earning between 81 and 100 percent of area median family income and are in compliance with Division 51A- 4.1100, as amended.

(b) Design standards. Compliance with 51A-4.1107 is not required. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, see Division 51A-13.400 for parking and loading regulations.

(b) Multifamily.

(1) In general. One space per dwelling unit is required.

(2) Guest parking. In addition to the requirement in Paragraph (1), an additional one-quarter space per dwelling unit is required to be provided for guest parking if the required parking in Paragraph (1) is restricted to resident parking only.

(3) Accessory use parking not required. No additional parking is required for accessory uses that are limited principally to resident use.

(c) Parking reduction for proximity to DART stations. The off-street parking requirement for uses located within one-third mile of a DART light-rail station may be reduced by up to 15 percent.

(d) Maximum surface parking. No more than seven percent of the area of a lot or building site may be used for surface parking. The director may increase the amount of surface parking to 15 percent of the area of a lot or building site if the director finds that:

(1) the surface parking area, other than ingress and egress points, does not directly abut a street frontage (for example, the surface parking is to the rear of the main structure); and

(2) the surface parking area has an enhanced perimeter buffer, as defined in Section 51A-10.126(b), between the surface parking area and the street. (Ord. 32601)

SEC. 51P- 1101.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32601)

SEC. 51P- 1101.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article XIII and with the frontage and open space plan.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(c) The planting zone must be a minimum of six feet.

(d) Except as provided in this subsection, one street tree must be provided for each 30 feet of frontage. Street trees must be located in the planting zones located within five feet of the street curb. Street trees may be planted in the required front yard as close as possible to the sidewalk if the city arborist determines there is a conflict with utilities, driveways, or visibility triangles.

(e) An enhanced buffer, as defined in Section 51A-10.126, is required between the Santa Fe Trail and any surface parking shown on the frontage and open space plan. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with Article XIII. (Ord. 32601)

sections.title: Open Space
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1101.114. OPEN SPACE.

(a) Purpose. Open space requirements are intended to:

(1) provide a main central focal point for the district and smaller focal points for the district;

(2) promote economic development;

(3) improve the quality of life of residents and visitors;

(4) provide relief from a dense urban environment;

(5) prevent concentrations of paved areas;

(6) improve air quality; and

(7) assist with pedestrian movement.

(b) In general. Except as provided in this section, the required open space must comply with the requirements for open space in Section 51A-13.303.

(c) Site plan. Compliance with open space requirements must be shown on a site plan and demonstrated at the time of application for any building permit for new construction or a major renovation.

(d) Minimum open space required. A minimum of 10 percent of a lot or building site must be maintained as open space. (Ord. 32601)

SEC. 51P-1101.114. STREET AND SIDEWALK STANDARDS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, streets, alleys, and driveways must be provided in accordance with Division 51A-13.500.

(b) Santa Fe Trail frontage.

(1) The Santa Fe Trail is not considered a primary street in accordance with Section 51A-13.703(c) but is considered as a primary street for the sole purpose of calculating open space, transparency, blank wall limitations, and required entrances as required by Section 51A-13.304.

(2) For the purposes of establishing setbacks and building frontage, the Santa Fe Trail is considered a rear yard.

(3) Vehicular access to the Santa Fe Trail is prohibited.

(c) Sidewalks.

(1) In general. Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk, subject to approval of the director. At each intersection of driveway and sidewalk, crosswalks must be constructed of a material that differs in finish and color from that of vehicular ingress and egress driveways. Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk, subject to approval of the director.

(2) Haskell Avenue. A sidewalk with an unobstructed width of six feet must be provided along Haskell Avenue.

(3) Streets other than Haskell Avenue. A sidewalk with a width of six feet must be provided along streets other than Haskell Avenue.

(4) Santa Fe Trail. There must be at least two access points to the Property from the Santa Fe Trail.

(d) Ash Street. The access drive/fire lane adjacent to Ash Street must terminate at least 50-feet from the Santa Fe Trail right-of-way if all fire protection requirements are met. If the access drive/fire lane must extend within 50 feet of the Santa Fe Trail right-of-way, a gate or bollards must be placed 50 feet from the Santa Fe Trail right-of-way to limit access to emergency vehicles only. (Ord. 32601)

SEC. 51P- 1101.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) In general.

(1) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(2) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(b) Sound attenuation.

(1) Housing units located within 1,000 feet and facing a freeway or light rail line must include standards for noise abatement and control to achieve an auditory environment not to exceed a day-night average sound level of 45 decibels within project bedrooms. The requirements imposed by this subsection address noise exposure associated with nearby traffic operations only. Architectural design measures used to produce this result may, but are not required to, include the following:

(A) site orientation or layout for buildings to serve as a noise shield;

(B) integration of a buffer, barrier, or open space or other site layout measures;

(C) building layout to consider location of exterior balconies and terraces to mitigate noise introduction into the building;

(D) exterior wall assemblies to include sound attenuation measures through wall construction and detailing; or

(E) exterior door and window specifications and detailing such as fully insulated and sealed perimeters.

(2) An environmental/architectural noise assessment and report must be provided to the director to confirm acceptable exterior-to-interior sound isolation and compliance with the 45 decibels limit. (Ord. 32601)

SEC. 51P- 1101.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32601)
